parties: Aegis Logistics Limited (transferor) and Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited (transferee, subsidiary)
headline: Aegis Logistics executes Business Transfer Agreement with subsidiary Aegis Terminal (Pipavav)
sum: Aegis Logistics Limited has executed a Business Transfer Agreement (BTA) with its subsidiary Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited, transferring terminal and logistics operations at Pipavav port. The transaction consolidates port operations within the Aegis group structure.
implication: Intra-group BTA between a listed parent and subsidiary triggers disclosure obligations under listing rules and may implicate transfer pricing scrutiny under the Income Tax Act; counsel must review the valuation mechanism, condition precedent approvals (including port authority and lender consent), and timing of effective date of transfer.
detail: Aegis Vopak Terminals Limited (a joint venture between Aegis Logistics and Royal Vopak) informed the NSE of the execution of a Business Transfer Agreement between its parent Aegis Logistics Limited and the subsidiary Aegis Terminal (Pipavav) Limited. The BTA effects a transfer of terminal operations and related business undertakings at the Pipavav port facility in Gujarat. As an intra-group transaction between a listed company and its subsidiary, this triggers materiality thresholds under SEBI Listing Regulations 2015 and requires board/shareholder approval and regulatory disclosure. The transaction likely includes transfer of assets, liabilities, contracts, and operational rights.
